key_insight: Autonomous vision-language evaluators can provide scalable reward signals for reinforcement learning in computer-use agents when their noise is explicitly corrected.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical RL fine-tuning for GUI agents in open-ended desktop environments without hand-crafted rewards or dense manual labeling.
method: Use the final screenshot and original instruction as the reward input to a vision-language model.
Treat evaluator output as a noisy binary terminal reward channel.
Apply a noise-corrected reward estimator inside PPO for policy optimization.
evidence_signal: Across macOSWorld, Windows Agent Arena, and OSWorld, corrected evaluator rewards improved success by 12.6 points over zero-shot and 5.1 points over raw evaluator fine-tuning.
watch_item: Performance depends on the evaluator’s accuracy, so miscalibration or domain shift in the vision-language judge can still bias reward learning.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
